FLEX.thesis_one_line: AI-datacenter cooling and power gear maker that is spinning off exactly that business into a separate company within about two quarters.
kill_criteria: RemainCo (post-spin) FY28 adjusted operating margin guidance, once disclosed, comes in below 6.0% (vs. 7.0-7.2% consolidated FY27 guide)
Consolidated net debt/EBITDA (EBITDA proxy: adjusted operating income + D&A) exceeds 2.0x at any quarter-end before the spin closes
Free cash flow conversion (FCF/adjusted net income) stays below 40% for two consecutive quarters
FY27 guidance is cut (not raised) at any of the next two quarterly releases
The CPI spin-off is delayed beyond Q2 calendar 2027 or restructured to retain more than 19.9% Flex ownership
key_adverse_facts: The Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment (JetCool liquid cooling, Anord Mardix, Crown Technical Systems) that drives the model's growth/margin-mix score is being spun off into an independent company (SpinCo) by Q1 CY2027, with Flex retaining at most 19.9% of SpinCo
Long-term debt nearly doubled in one quarter (Mar-26 $3,751M to Jun-26 $5,219M) to fund the $1,134M Electrical Power Products acquisition
Free cash flow fell to $41M in Q1 FY27 from $268M a year earlier (FCF/adjusted net income ~11%)
August 2025 missile strike on the Mukachevo, Ukraine facility caused $51M of FY26 asset impairments/write-downs
data_conflicts: Triage's stated rationale (durable margin-mix shift toward datacenter power/cooling) does not account for the fact that this exact segment is contractually scheduled to leave the FLEX ticker via spin-off; the triage's own red flag ('monitor whether the mix shift is durable') understates the issue, which is structural/corporate-action risk, not just cyclical durability
FLEX.confidence_in_thesis: med (guidance momentum and revenue growth are well documented in primary filings; next-earnings date is an estimate based on the prior-year Q2 FY26 release date of Oct 29, 2025, not yet confirmed by an official Flex announcement, and exact FY28 RemainCo economics were not disclosed in the sources reviewed)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for FLEX; my own reverse DCF implies a 10-year FCF CAGR of about 10.6% at the 2026-09-25 close, slightly above my 9% base case, so the stock is priced at the full end of fair value even before the spin-off structural risk is weighed in.

FLEX.scenario_basis: Base: FY26 FCF $1,060M run-rate growing ~9%/yr, exit at ~14x FCF (below current ~29x EV/FCF, reflecting post-spin RemainCo de-rating toward historical EMS multiples), no dividend; bear: FCF stagnant near $1.0-1.1B and multiple compresses to ~10x on spin execution risk; bull: RemainCo content plus SpinCo stake value both compound, multiple holds near 18x.

INTC.thesis_one_line: x86 and AI-chip maker with a real revenue inflection and government-backed funding, but its foundry still loses billions and the stock's price implies a turnaround far beyond any case the filings support.
kill_criteria: Intel Foundry quarterly operating loss exceeds $2.5 billion for two consecutive quarters (vs. $2.089B in Q2 2026)
Consolidated net debt exceeds $30 billion at any quarter-end (vs. approximately $20.8B at Jun-26)
Q3 2026 revenue comes in below the guided $15.8 billion low end
The escrowed-share derivative liability produces a further single-quarter loss exceeding $5 billion
External (non-Intel) 18A/14A foundry customer revenue fails to appear as a disclosed, named line item within the next four quarters
key_adverse_facts: Intel Foundry lost $2,089 million in Q2 2026 despite 31% segment revenue growth, confirming the triage's own red flag

The $(11.0) billion GAAP net loss in Q2 2026 was driven by a $12.5 billion non-cash loss on the fair-value change of Escrowed Shares owed to the U.S. Department of Commerce under the Secure Enclave/CHIPS Act agreement -- a mechanism that worsens as Intel's own stock price rises
Total Intel stockholders' equity fell by $26.7 billion in six months (Dec-25 to Jun-26), driven mainly by this escrow-related loss
A Delaware Court of Chancery shareholder derivative suit (filed March 5, 2026) alleges the board breached fiduciary duty in approving the $11 billion U.S. government equity stake

The U.S. government holds warrants for 241 million shares at $20.00 that become exercisable if Intel's ownership of its foundry business falls below 51%, constraining future foundry-divestiture options
data_conflicts: The triage's cited news sources (CNBC, JonPeddie) do not explain that the headline GAAP net loss is a non-operating, non-cash escrow-derivative revaluation rather than an operating deterioration; read in isolation the GAAP loss looks far worse than the underlying Products-segment performance
INTC.confidence_in_thesis: low (the Products-segment growth is well documented, but the escrow-liability mechanism, litigation accrual figures, and the true normalized FCF base are not fully verified from primary sources in this pass, the reverse DCF could not be bracketed within a 30% 10-year FCF CAGR ceiling, and the Oct 22, 2026 earnings date is an unconfirmed estimate, not an official Intel announcement)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for INTC; my reverse DCF at the 2026-09-25 close and a ~$620B market cap could not find a 10-year FCF CAGR under 30% that would justify the EV against a generous $3B/yr normalized FCF base, so the price requires a materially more optimistic outcome than my base case.

INTC.scenario_basis: Base: Foundry losses persist near current run-rate, Products segment grows high-single-digits, normalized FCF stays near $2-4B/yr against a ~$620B market cap, multiple compresses as the turnaround story matures without a foundry breakeven; bear: 18A external yield/ramp disappoints, Foundry losses widen, further escrow-liability volatility; bull: 18A/14A ramp succeeds, external foundry customers materialize, Foundry approaches breakeven by 2028.

JBL.thesis_one_line: Electronics manufacturer riding real AI-datacenter demand with guidance raised twice running, but its equity cushion has been run thin by buybacks funding a highly leveraged balance sheet.
kill_criteria: Core operating margin (Non-GAAP) falls below 5.0% for two consecutive quarters (vs. 5.8% FQ3 FY26 actual and 5.8% FY26 full-year guide)
Total Jabil Inc. stockholders' equity (consolidated) falls below $1.0 billion at any quarter-end
Net debt (notes payable and long-term debt, less cash) exceeds $3.5 billion at any quarter-end (vs. approximately $2.0B at May-26)
FY26 or FY27 guidance is cut (not raised) versus the immediately prior range at any quarterly release
Adjusted free cash flow conversion (adjusted FCF divided by core earnings) falls below 70% for two consecutive quarters
key_adverse_facts: Total Jabil Inc. stockholders' equity fell from $1,513M (Aug-25) to $1,323M (May-26) even as total assets grew from $18.5B to $23.8B, pushing assets/equity leverage from about 12.2x to 18.0x in nine months

Nine-month cash paid for acquisitions was $852 million (including the Hanley Energy Group deal), funded mostly by new borrowings of $2,144 million, roughly doubling goodwill and intangible assets in nine months
Core EMS margins remain thin in absolute terms (GAAP operating margin 5.1% in FQ3 FY26) despite the improving trend
JBL.confidence_in_thesis: med (revenue, margin and guidance trends are well documented from two consecutive primary-source earnings releases; the FQ4 FY26/full-year release is officially confirmed for Sept 30, 2026 per Jabil's own investor-relations announcement, just after the 2026-09-25 cutoff, and was not yet available to review in this pass)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for JBL; my reverse DCF implies a 10-year FCF CAGR of about 10.3% at the 2026-09-25 close (secondary-source price cross-check), roughly in line with my 11% base case, supporting a small-weight include rather than a full-weight one given the balance-sheet reservation.

JBL.scenario_basis: Base: adjusted FCF run-rate ~$1.32B/yr (nine-month $991M annualized) growing ~11%/yr as AI-infrastructure content keeps expanding, exit multiple near current ~18x NTM P/E, no meaningful dividend (nine-month dividends paid only $27M); bear: AI-capex cycle cools, core margin reverts toward 2.6% as triage flagged, multiple compresses toward 12x; bull: core margin sustains above 6.5% and multiple holds near 22x on continued guidance raises.
